title: Atomic-6 Space Armor debris shield flies

research.what: The Whipple shield, a sacrificial bumper that breaks up fast debris before it reaches a spacecraft wall, is the conceptual origin of modern debris shielding. Origin: Fred Whipple's meteoroid bumper shield concept, 1947. This is a conceptual origin only: I found no named paper or patent for Atomic-6's own composite tile.

change.what: Atomic-6's composite Space Armor tiles were launched on Portal Space Systems' Starburst-1 on 20–21 October 2026 (Falcon 9, Bandwagon-5). The company describes this as their first operational deployment in orbit after ground hypervelocity testing.

note: This is the first in-orbit use of a lightweight composite debris shield that is also transparent to radio signals. The research lineage is loose, and the mission is a one-year flight demonstration rather than a commercial fleet rollout.
